title: Chapter 29.  Media, Communications & Press Freedom in J&K

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom, is derived from Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution, subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).
The Jammu & Kashmir Media Policy 2020 was promulgated to streamline government advertisements, enhance media outreach, and curb fake news in the Union Territory.
In the landmark Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) ruling, the Supreme Court held that freedom of speech and trade over the internet is constitutionally protected.
The Directorate of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) serves as the primary government nodal agency for press communications and accreditation in J&K.

blocks.content: Freedom of speech and expression through the medium of the internet is an integral part of Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.

items: Supreme Court ruling in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India established that indefinite internet suspensions are illegal and subject to judicial review.
The Media Policy 2020 empowers DIPR to monitor content for fake news and security concerns before issuing official advertisements.
Article 19(2) allows the State to impose reasonable restrictions on press freedom on grounds of sovereignty, integrity, and public order.
